name: Black Moonstone
emotional: Offers a sense of safe depth
physical: Associated with a sense of steadiness
Kept nearby for comfort in stressful times
summary: Black Moonstone is a dark, silvery feldspar prized for grounded intuition, shadow work and protection, a deeper cousin of classic moonstone.
intro: Black moonstone is a dark grey to near-black feldspar that carries a silvery or blue-white shimmer drifting across its surface. The base stone is often a moonstone with dense inclusions, and some commercial material is a dark feldspar that has been treated or dyed to deepen the color. When it is cut as a cabochon and rotated under a lamp, a ghostly sheen glides over the dark body, which is why it is so loved by jewelers who like moody designs. Mining centers include India, Madagascar, and Sri Lanka. It feels heavier and stiller than pale moonstone, like a quiet night rather than a bright full Moon.
history: Black moonstone is a modern trade name rather than an ancient gem with its own history. It belongs to the moonstone family, a group long treasured in India, Sri Lanka, and the Mediterranean world as stones of the Moon. Dark, shimmering feldspars were once simply described as grey moonstone, and only as crystal markets grew in recent decades did black moonstone become a distinct product. Some stones sold under the name are actually labradorite or treated feldspar, which is why buyers should ask about the source. Its lore in modern crystal circles borrows from the dark side of the Moon: new Moon work, shadow exploration, and quiet protection.
meaning: Where pale moonstone speaks to dreamy intuition, black moonstone is said to ground that intuition in the body. Practitioners link it to the Root and Earth Star chakras as well as the Third Eye, describing a stone that lets you explore difficult feelings without drifting away. It is a classic companion for shadow work and for new Moon rituals, when the night sky is dark and intentions are planted. People also keep it as a quiet protector in busy or draining environments, believing it softens the edges of other people's moods. Its energy is described as steady, deep, and patient. Many find it helpful during periods of change, when they want to feel rooted and still trust their instincts. Cancer natives, ruled by the Moon, are often drawn to its depth.
howToUse: Hold black moonstone during evening meditation and watch the silvery sheen move as a gentle focus. Keep a pocket stone to feel steadier on busy days. Place one by your journal during shadow-work sessions or new Moon intention setting. In a grid, set it at the base to anchor lighter stones like clear quartz or rainbow moonstone. Wear it as a ring or pendant for subtle protection and grounded intuition. Some people set a small piece near the front door as a quiet guardian for the home.
care: Black moonstone is Mohs 6 to 6.5 and carries the cleavage typical of feldspars, so avoid knocks and store it apart from harder stones. A quick lukewarm rinse is fine, but dry it promptly and skip ultrasonic cleaners. Cleanse with moonlight, sound, or smoke. If your stone is dyed, avoid soaking, which may release color. Recharge on a windowsill at the new or full Moon. Keep away from sudden heat and harsh chemicals.
identify: Genuine black moonstone has a dark body with a floating silver or blue-white sheen that shifts with movement. Stones sold as black moonstone may actually be labradorite with a dark body or dyed feldspar, so ask for the source. Black glass shows a fixed glare and bubbles, and black onyx or agate lacks any moving sheen. Dyed stones may rub color onto a damp cloth and show a flat, uniform black without internal depth.

faq.q: What is black moonstone used for?
faq.a: Black moonstone is traditionally used for grounded intuition, shadow work, and protection. People hold it in meditation or keep it nearby during new Moon rituals when they want to feel steady and explore their inner world.

Genuine moonstone does exist in dark grey and near-black shades, but some stones sold under the name are labradorite or dyed feldspar. Ask the seller about the origin and check for a moving sheen that glides across the surface.

faq.q: How is black moonstone different from regular moonstone?
faq.a: Regular moonstone is pale with a blue-white glow and is linked to dreamy intuition. Black moonstone is darker and is said to ground that intuition, supporting shadow work, boundaries, and a feeling of quiet protection.
